newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks led up by banks in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks led up by banks in sluggish trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks edged higher led by bank stocks in markets still sluggish after the Christmas and New Year break.

Bogota's IBB index closed 0.15 percent up at 844.41 amid a 281 million peso volume, limited to just seven stocks. Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 0.32 percent closing at 13,466.54 amid a 679 million peso volume, in a session where just six different stocks were traded.
"It's obvious the markets are still affected by the New Year holidays when many shareholders and brokers leave the city and switch off from business," one Bogota broker said.

On the Bogota exchange, Banco de Colombia rose 0.72 percent to 418. The bulk of the session's volume was concentrated in brewing giant Bavaria, which ended unchanged at 4,100 in total trade of 142 million pesos.
Bancoquia bank, in which Spain's Grupo Santander will shortly complete the purchase of a 55 percent stake, fell back 2.72 percent to 2,500.

Banco Ganadero climbed 5.47 percent to 270 on the Medellin exchange amid a flurry of demand from small investors. The day's volume was concentrated in a 445 million peso trade in supermarket chain Almacenes Exito, unchanged at 3,100.

"We don't think the 1996 inflation figure will be good news for the stock market because it means interest rates are likely to remain high. That means investors are unlikely to turn their gaze to the stock market for the time being at least," another Bogot broker said.
The National Statistics Department announced the consumer price index rose 21.63 percent in 1996, outstripping the government target of 17 percent.
